releases.notes:
# ZPBW 1.0.1 — Minecraft 26.2

## Fixes

### Mining and interactions

- Keep queued mining and its swing together after warp confirmation, with physics using the updated block state.
- Cancel mining against changed or missing blocks and recheck the target before replay.
- Prevent held mining from accumulating multiple progress updates in one tick; clear queued mining on world/connection changes.

### Prediction and recovery

- Fix first-warp predictions when sneak was pressed but had not yet been sent to the server. NoSneakDelay remains supported.
- Discard obsolete movement/input ticks after a failed prediction while preserving inventory synchronization.
- Refresh the interaction target after rollback and restore input, sprint and hotbar tracking when buffered actions are cancelled.
- Add dispatched use angles and movement context to `/zpbw logs` for diagnosing airborne prediction mismatches.

### Standalone SkyBlock detection

- Remove the optional Blackwell lookup and developer override dependency.
- Read full sidebar text, tab headers/footers and rendered player names directly from Minecraft.
- Handle formatted text and Unicode spacing; ignore empty or decorative area labels.

## Verification and remaining limits

- 202 automated mod tests pass. Gameplay fixes were exercised in the owned Grim lab at 25–300 ms latency, including mining, interactions, recovery, jumps and Jump Boost V.
- The new detector passed automated checks and mapping verification; a minimal-client/live SkyBlock runtime check has not been completed.
- Five-warp chaining still pauses new dispatch after the first confirmation until the remaining chain settles. Timeout still counts nonzero server Ping packets; bursts can exhaust its budget. General airborne prediction mismatches remain under investigation.

## Installation

Requires Minecraft 26.2, Java 25, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API and Fabric Language Kotlin. No other SkyBlock mod is required.

Replace the older ZPBW JAR with `zpbw-1.0.1.jar` and restart Minecraft. Existing settings are preserved. Run `/zpbw logs` after a problem to collect a troubleshooting report.

releases.notes:
# ZPBW 1.0.0 — Minecraft 26.2

Zero Ping Blinkwarp predicts supported etherwarp destinations locally and keeps camera and movement responsive while waiting for the real server teleport. Dependent actions stay in order until confirmation.

## Installation

Requires Minecraft Java 26.2, Java 25, Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or newer, Fabric API and Fabric Language Kotlin.

Download `zpbw-1.0.0.jar`, remove any older standalone ZPBW JAR from your `mods` folder, and install this one. Existing settings are preserved. Restart Minecraft after replacing the JAR.

## Getting started

- Run `/zpbw` for the command list and `/zpbw on` to enable prediction.
- `/zpbw nsd` toggles NoSneakDelay; both features default to off on a fresh installation.
- `/zpbw timeout <ticks>` sets the confirmation timeout, clamped to 2–20 server Ping packets (default 20).
- `/zpbw logs` copies session diagnostics for a [bug report](https://github.com/hawkzlol/zpbw/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml).
- Newer stable releases are checked once per client session; notifications appear after joining SkyBlock. No automatic downloads or installation.

## Notes

Up to five unconfirmed warps can overlap. After the first confirmation, new dispatch briefly waits for the rest of that chain to settle. Prediction uses the world visible to your client and can differ from the server. Queued interactions still depend on server confirmation; network latency itself remains.

The release passes 174 standalone tests and Windows/Linux CI. Earlier local lab testing covered latency, chains, interactions and recovery; it does not establish every live-server/mod combination or guarantee freedom from bans.

The attached SHA-256 file identifies the release JAR. Review copied diagnostics before sharing: they include positions, timings and mod versions.
